items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: My cousin was playing drums before. I got big enough to play drums. And his name? Charlie Watson.

ctx.x: Who was in your daddy's band? Did he have a band of his own or what?

Yeah, he had a band of his own. He had a fellow by the name of Joe Davis playing guitar. A fellow by the name of Selby Thomas on, uh, bass. Uh, uh, what's his trumpet player name? Uh, Moulier Melanson. He was on trumpet. And, uh, I was on drums. My cousin was playing drums before. I got big enough to play drums. And his name? Charlie Watson. And, uh, who else? At that time, they wasn't usually getting, I mean, no piano. And then... Trombone? Well, trombone and a fellow by the name of, uh, Frank Toes playing…

As a matter of fact, his son's playing trombone somewhere around Memphis. Do you know his son's name? They call him Wash. I don't know his other name. All I know is Wash. Did you name a clarinet player with your father's family? No. No, he didn't have one?

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: A drummer by the name of Charlie Watson.

ctx.x: A.J. What band did your daddy play with? I mean, do you remember any of the bands you played with? Yeah, they were on the orchestra. You ever been in line with that?

A.J. Handy's band. Yeah. I had a bass player by the name of Selby Thomas. A trumpet player by the name of Moie Melonso. A drummer by the name of Charlie Watson. A guitar player by the name of Willie Davis, but everybody called him Pick. And who else? A trombone player, Frank Toads. And then later I started playing drums with him. I played drums with him for about three years. A.J. What kind of band was it? A.J. The jazz band. A red time band they called him at the time. A.J. Did they read music? No, no, no. The…
And he had the band here, you were dating, you know? Yeah. They didn't grind at all into play? No, from here, from here in the movie he went.
